My own note history (dir_accuracy 0.463) says I have no directional edge here, so I will keep convictions low and reason only about trend-gate discipline, which IS validated on this market.

theses.subject: AI Infrastructure
theses.thesis: AI Infrastructure remains the leader and passes the absolute-trend eligibility gate (eligible=true), and the validated edge here is staying-power/volatility control, not return forecasting. Breadth is thin (0.125), so this reads as concentrated leadership rather than broad participation — which supports a tilt only with the trend-gate protection already applied by the allocator.

theses.subject: US Energy Complex
theses.thesis: Energy is the challenger (rank 2, score 1.375) and passes the eligibility gate with genuinely broad participation (breadth 0.636, the widest of any top theme) and a moderately high durability bar. The narrowing rotation and thin leader margin make Energy the more cohesive trend candidate on breadth, even though it is not the leader.
theses.dissent: It is not the leader — buying the challenger on a rotation structure is implicitly guessing at a handoff, which the detector explicitly warns has no validated forward edge.

falsifier.text: XLE underperforms AI Infrastructure (SMH) by more than 5% over a rolling 15-day window before the check-by date.

theses.subject: Cybersecurity
theses.thesis: Cybersecurity (CIBR) is eligible and high-ranked but sits at crowded=true with crowding_z 1.61, the highest crowding flag among top eligibles. Per the detector rules this is a size-down caution, not a short — but as a lean, I would simply not add exposure here while the crowding texture is this stretched.

falsifier.text: CIBR's crowding_z drops below 1.0 while it remains eligible and ranked in the top 5.
